title: Assam GK — Quick Facts and Static GK Compendium

blocks.content: Assam GK — Quick Facts and Static GK Compendium
Consolidates high-frequency, exact-recall static facts about Assam into a single quick-revision chapter — ideal for last-minute review before any Assam-focused exam.

items: Capital — Dispur (within the Guwahati metropolitan area); Largest city — Guwahati.
State Legislature — Unicameral Assam Legislative Assembly; High Court — Gauhati High Court.
Major rivers — Brahmaputra (main valley), Barak (southern valley); Majuli — one of the world's largest river islands, in the Brahmaputra.
International borders — Bhutan (north), Bangladesh (south); connected to mainland India via the Siliguri Corridor through West Bengal.
State animal — Great Indian One-Horned Rhinoceros; State bird — White-winged Wood Duck; State tree — Hollong (Dipterocarpus macrocarpus); State flower — Foxtail Orchid (Kopou Phul).
Ahom dynasty founded — 1228 CE, by Sukaphaa; Ahom rule duration — approximately 600 years (until 1826).
Battle of Saraighat — 1671, Ahom victory over the Mughals led by Lachit Borphukan.
Treaty of Yandabo — 1826, ceded Assam to British control, ending the First Anglo-Burmese War.
First Chief Minister of Assam (post-independence) — Gopinath Bordoloi.
Assam Company (first commercial tea enterprise) — established 1839.
Three Bihu festivals — Rongali/Bohag Bihu (April, New Year), Kongali/Kati Bihu (October), Bhogali/Magh Bihu (January, harvest).
Sattriya dance — one of India's eight classical dance forms, originating from Assam's satra tradition.
Muga silk — unique golden-hued silk variety native to Assam, GI-tagged; Sualkuchi — major silk-weaving centre near Guwahati.
Digboi — site of Asia's first oil well/refinery, Upper Assam.

Kaziranga National Park — UNESCO World Heritage Site, home to the world's largest population of the one-horned rhinoceros; Manas National Park — UNESCO World Heritage Site and Tiger Reserve on the Assam-Bhutan border.
Sixth Schedule Autonomous Councils in Assam — Karbi Anglong Autonomous Council, Dima Hasao (North Cachar Hills) Autonomous Council, Bodoland Territorial Council (BTC/BTR).
Assam Public Service Commission (APSC) — the state's primary recruitment examination body, analogous to the UPSC at the central level.
Barak Valley districts — Cachar, Karimganj, Hailakandi; principal town — Silchar.

cells:
Exam Tip

• This chapter is designed as a final-week revision tool — read through it repeatedly in the days before an exam rather than as a first-pass learning resource, since it assumes the detailed context from earlier chapters is already familiar.

• State symbols (animal, bird, tree, flower) are simple, guaranteed-value questions that are frequently skipped in preparation — a few minutes memorizing this short list yields disproportionate returns.

• Cross-reference any fact here against the corresponding detailed chapter if you feel uncertain — this compendium is meant to reinforce, not replace, the fuller explanations earlier in the book.
